title: Juan Garrido, from Kongo to Baja California
summary: Born about 1480 in the Kingdom of Kongo, taken to Lisbon about 1495 and in Santo Domingo by 1502–03, Juan Garrido served in Puerto Rico, Florida and Cuba, then in Mexico with Cortés. He sowed the first wheat harvested in New Spain, led a gold-mining crew to Zacatula, sailed on Cortés's Pacific venture, and in 1538 petitioned the Crown for the pension his thirty years had earned. Where the sources give no route the legs are a broad brush.

legs.source: History Workshop, The Story of Juan Garrido: to Lisbon about 1495
legs.note: No source gives the route or the port; the line is the usual way up the African coast. Birthplace: Kongo per Wikipedia and History Workshop, "West Africa" per NPS

legs.source: NPS, Juan Garrido: by Seville and a convoy to Hispaniola
legs.note: The year is 1502 or 1503 by the sources; NPS has him leave Lisbon for Seville in 1503

legs.source: NPS, Juan Garrido: with Ponce de León to Puerto Rico
Wikipedia, Juan Garrido: in Velázquez's conquest of Cuba
legs.note: A bridging leg, north about Hispaniola; no source gives the route

legs.source: Wikipedia, Juan Garrido: in Velázquez's conquest of Cuba
legs.note: Wikipedia dates his part in the conquest of Cuba to 1508, earlier than the conquest itself (1511–14); the sources say only that he took part, and the line across the island, east to west, is a broad brush

legs.source: Wikipedia, Juan Garrido; Hernán Cortés (Wikipedia): Cortés sailed from Cuba in February 1519, by Yucatán and Tabasco, and his men took Veracruz in July
legs.note: The route is Cortés's fleet. Some authors have Garrido arrive a year later with the contingent of Pánfilo de Narváez, joining Cortés after the Narváez men abandoned him

legs.source: Hernán Cortés (Wikipedia): received by Moctezuma II on 8 Nov 1519
History Workshop, The Story of Juan Garrido: leads a gold-mining crew of enslaved African men to Zacatula
legs.note: Zacatula is the sources' name for a place on the Pacific coast; the road there is a broad brush

legs.source: History Workshop, The Story of Juan Garrido: with Cortés from 1533
legs.note: No source read names the port Cortés sailed from; the coast drawn is a guess

legs.source: History Workshop, The Story of Juan Garrido: the venture to Baja California took roughly 300 enslaved Black people
legs.note: Dates are 1533–36 per History Workshop and 1533 per NPS. The landing mark stands at the Bay of La Paz, the usual identification; the sources read do not name it

events.label: Puerto Rico: gold, and a revolt
events.text: In 1508 he joined Ponce de León in the search for gold on Puerto Rico, and in 1511 fought with the Spanish against the Native peoples who rose in revolt.

events.label: Florida with Ponce de León
events.text: Garrido sailed with Ponce de León's expedition that found La Florida. They claimed the land and left when they could not subdue the people there.

events.label: Florida, 1521: not drawn
events.text: NPS has him return to Florida with Ponce de León in 1521, the voyage on which Ponce was fatally wounded. Wikipedia and History Workshop place him at Tenochtitlan that year, so no line is drawn here.

events.label: Tenochtitlan: the dead gathered, a chapel built
events.text: He survived the slaughter of Cortés's troops. NPS says he helped collect the soldiers' remains; Wikipedia says he built a chapel that year for the Spaniards killed in the fighting, now the church of San Hipólito.

events.label: Mexico City: the first wheat
events.source: History Workshop, The Story of Juan Garrido
events.text: He sowed the first wheat in New Spain, on the edge of the city, and Matthew Restall credits him with the first harvest in New Spain. NPS has him granted land on a dried-up lake in 1522, History Workshop a house plot only in 1525. Cortés claimed he had ordered the sowing; Garrido denied it.

events.label: Zacatula: a gold-mining crew
events.source: History Workshop, The Story of Juan Garrido
events.text: He led a group of enslaved African men on a gold-mining expedition to Zacatula.

events.label: The probanza: thirty years of service
events.source: History Workshop, The Story of Juan Garrido
events.text: He wrote to Charles V to ask for a pension: "I, Juan Garrido, black resident of this city". He was later paid in land and money.
